title: Collective surfing of single cells on a chemo-attractant wave using multiscale Eulerian velocity vector field

key_results: Single cells show ~180° antipodal phase relationship to cAMP wave velocity fields; cells surf the wave crest and rest in troughs with randomized directionality

model_io.model: UV-C wave interference on reflective surface

hypotheses.hypothesis: Electromagnetic wave interference creates stable exposure minima near reflective surfaces that protect pathogens

comments: Demonstrates that GCS is a genuine superconducting phenomenon beyond transport; spatially-resolved imaging provides constraints on microscopic mechanisms.

model_io.model: Scanning NV-center magnetometer at sub-Kelvin temperatures

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gate control of supercurrents manifests in Meissner suppression via quasiparticle generation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; hot-spot model consistent with imaging, other mechanisms ruled out

title: Resolving Abrikosov vortex entry in superconducting nanostring resonators via displacement-noise spectroscopy in cavity optomechanics
task: Resolve single Abrikosov vortex entry in superconducting nanostring via cavity optomechanics
key_results: Discrete frequency jumps attributed to single/few-vortex entry with pinning energies 0.09–0.44 eV; collective Labusch parameter ~10¹⁴ N m⁻⁴; attonewton-scale force resolution
comments: Demonstrates optomechanical sensing as sensitive probe of vortex matter; disorder-mediated nucleation and Campbell–Labusch response cleanly separated, enabling quantitative vortex pinning landscape characterization.

model_io.model: Cavity optomechanical platform: suspended Al nanostring SQUID
Single-event pinning model + Campbell–Labusch elastic response

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nanomechanical elastic signatures resolve stochastic vortex entry and distinguish pinning from collective elastic response
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; frequency jumps correlate with single-vortex entry, smooth background identified with Labusch elasticity

title: Rotational wobble effects on equilibrium structure and Floquet stability in the circular restricted three body problem
task: Quantify perturbations to circular restricted three-body problem from primary rotational wobble
key_results: Periodic wobble shifts libration points by analytical perturbation result; Floquet analysis shows systematic stability modifications; trajectory deviations reach 10⁵–10⁶ m over long integration for Sun–Earth system
comments: Physically motivated extension to CR3BP; results highlight importance of higher-order dynamics for precision astrodynamics, though wobble amplitude and mass asymmetry must be measured independently.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rotational wobble induces persistent time-dependent equilibrium shifts and cumulative trajectory deviations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; analytical perturbation theory and numerical integration show deviations up to 10⁶ m

title: Experimental and numerical study of the effect of appurtenances on the wind-induced vibrations of a cable-stayed bridge
task: Assess wind-induced vibration response of cable-stayed bridge across construction and completion stages
key_results: Drag force increases 20%, lift decreases 64%, rolling moment increases 52% from construction to completion; vertical displacement/acceleration decrease up to 79%/40% during construction; lateral acceleration increases 69% at completion; soft flutter observed at α=−3°; critical wind speed >108 m/s
comments: Stage-dependent aerodynamic and dynamic behavior is crucial for lifecycle safety; numerical-experimental divergence at high wind speeds on completed bridge suggests nonlinear effects or model limitations.

model_io.model: Integrated numerical (static wind loads + buffeting + self-excited forces) and wind tunnel experimental approach

hypotheses.hypothesis: Appurtenances and completion stage dramatically alter aerodynamic sensitivity and dynamic stability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; construction phase more vulnerable vertically, completion phase laterally; stage-specific design constraints identified

title: Design of topological thermal diffusion in the quasi ballistic phonon regime
task: Design topological thermal diffusion in quasi-ballistic phonon regime at nanoscale
key_results: Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model extended to nanoscale thermal transport with size-dependent effective conductivity; predicted decay rates agree with experiments within model uncertainties
comments: Bridges topological design principles with quasi-ballistic phonon physics; provides practical engineering framework but validation limited to localized states.

model_io.model: Effective diffusion-based topological framework for Si nanostructures
outputs: decay rate of topological interface states

hypotheses.hypothesis: Topological diffusion can robustly function in quasi-ballistic phonon regime when size-dependent conductivity is incorporated
hypotheses.result: Supported; predicted rates match measurements for strongly localized states
